title: The trajectory as data: turns, log-probabilities, snapshots and a deterministic replay
design_ref: The trajectory as data: turns, snapshots and branch points
purpose: Run the policy on all 32 tasks, four attempts each, as primary rollouts. Then look at one trajectory as the store holds it, and replay it from one of its snapshots to check that the environment is deterministic: the same state and actions give the same observations.

steps.display: branch points chosen across all 128 trajectories, by reason

checks.because: One Indexed Job of 12 pods; each pod runs every 12th attempt and writes each trajectory through the store.

checks.description: every turn has its context, its per-token log-probabilities from the rollout engine, its policy version and the environment's checks
checks.because: The runner stores the exact message list and the token ids with their log-probabilities for every turn; the verifier computes the checks on the real files.

checks.description: only some turns are branch points, chosen by uncertainty, by important actions, or every third turn
checks.because: A snapshot is taken only at a branch point; the reason is recorded with it.

checks.description: replaying from the snapshot reproduced every observation and every state hash
checks.because: Observations have no clock or path in them (test timings are removed), listings are sorted, and snapshots are byte-for-byte deterministic.
